channel.title: Al Beltran — Engineering Journal
channel.description: Engineering notes and interview prep by Al Andrew Paul Beltran. Published articles only.

item.title: TypeScript Interview Questions, With the Reasoning
item.description: Types at boundaries, narrowing, generics, and the questions that separate autocomplete from design.

item.title: TypeScript as an API Contract, Not a Costume
item.description: Share types across producer and consumer, validate at the edge, and stop trusting JSON because it compiled once.

item.title: System Design Interview Questions, With the Reasoning
item.description: A small set of design prompts with the tradeoffs interviewers listen for — not a 50-box diagram.

item.title: SQL Interview Questions, With the Reasoning
item.description: Joins, indexes, NULL, and transactions — answered the way a production engineer talks about plans.

item.title: React Interview Questions, With the Reasoning
item.description: A compact React interview set: hooks, rendering, state, and architecture — with what interviewers are actually scoring.

item.title: A Mental Model for React Hooks That Survives Production
item.description: Treat hooks as subscriptions to render, not lifecycle methods with new names. The model that prevents stale state and mystery effects.

item.title: Node.js Interview Questions, With the Reasoning
item.description: The event loop, errors, streams, and production habits — not a list of module names.

item.title: AWS Lambda Failure Modes You Should Budget For
item.description: Timeouts, retries, partial batch failure, and the handler that is not idempotent.

item.title: JavaScript Interview Questions, With the Reasoning
item.description: Closures, the event loop, equality, and this — explained as runtime behavior, not trivia.

item.title: The AEM Author–Developer Contract
item.description: A component is successful when an author can use it without a Slack thread. Dialogs, names, and defaults are the product.

item.title: When the GPU Vendor Owns the Model Hub
item.description: If the company that sells the chips also owns the default place engineers pull open models, pinning, licensing, and exit plans stop being theoretical.

item.title: Your Agent Is Missing the Monitoring Layer the Labs Shipped
item.description: Frontier models are being wrapped in eval gates and misalignment monitors. Most product agents still log prompts and hope. That gap is now the production problem.

item.title: SQLite Is Back, and the Edge Is Why
item.description: D1, Turso, LiteFS, and a decade of Postgres-by-default have teams rediscovering a file database. The win is locality. The bill is replication and migration discipline.

item.title: Why Most RAG Demos Die in Production
item.description: Retrieval-augmented generation looks finished in a notebook. In production it is a search problem, a freshness problem, and an evaluation problem wearing a chat UI.

item.title: Idempotency Keys Are the Real API Contract
item.description: Retries are not an edge case. If a client can double-submit a payment, a reward, or a provision call, the header that names the attempt is the interface.

item.title: Post-Quantum TLS Is an Operations Problem
item.description: Hybrid key exchange is landing in browsers and CDNs. The engineering work is inventory, dual-stack certificates, and not breaking the middleboxes you forgot you had.

item.title: Platform Engineering Is Not a Portal
item.description: A golden path is paved workflows, paved defaults, and a team that owns the pavement. A catalog of links with a search bar is a bookmark manager.

item.title: Serverless Still Has a Latency Budget
item.description: Managed functions removed capacity planning. They did not remove tail latency, cold starts, or the cost of chatty downstreams. You still have a budget. It is just itemized differently.

item.title: Observability Without SLOs Is Expensive Logging
item.description: Dashboards that cannot tell you whether to wake someone up are decoration. Start from the user promise, then buy traces.

item.title: TypeScript Won the Integration Layer
item.description: The interesting TypeScript story is not frontend fashion. It is the language teams use to glue APIs, workers, and infrastructure code that used to be a pile of untyped scripts.

item.title: CSS Finally Caught Up to the Layout We Hacked
item.description: Container queries, :has(), and nested CSS removed a generation of JavaScript measuring hacks. The remaining work is restraint: not every layout needs a new primitive.

item.title: Feature Flags Beat Long-Lived Branches
item.description: A flag in production is a smaller, reversible risk than a branch that only exists on one laptop. Trunk-based delivery is an operations choice, not a Git fashion.

item.title: Supply Chain Security Is a Runtime Problem Now
item.description: xz and a decade of npm incidents taught the same lesson: you run other people's code. Pinning, provenance, and a small dependency graph beat a PDF named policy.

item.title: The SPA Hangover and What Server Components Are For
item.description: Client-rendered apps solved a 2015 shipping problem. They also shipped empty shells and waterfalls. Server Components are a boundary tool, not a rewrite religion.

item.title: Local-First Sync Is a Product Problem
item.description: CRDTs and sync engines are impressive. Users still need a story for conflict, offline writes, and what happens when two cashiers sell the last seat.

item.title: SQL Is Still the Skill That Compounds
item.description: Models can draft a query. They cannot own the index, the cardinality, or the 2 a.m. plan that scans the wrong partition. Relational literacy is still leverage.

item.title: Rate Limits Are Product Design
item.description: 429s are not just a WAF rule. They encode who gets capacity, what a client should do next, and whether your API is a partner or a trap.

item.title: Wasm on the Server Is a Boundary Tool
item.description: WebAssembly in the data center is useful when you need isolation, multi-language plugins, or a portable sandbox. It is not a replacement for a well-run service.

item.title: Designing Event-Driven Loyalty Rewards for Card Activation
item.description: How an activation-to-reward pipeline using SQS, SNS, Lambda, and Talon.One keeps fintech loyalty flows decoupled and operable.

item.title: Event Sourcing Without the Religion
item.description: An event log is a tool for audit and replay. It is not a requirement for every domain object. Most systems need durable facts and a projection, not a conference architecture.

item.title: WebGPU Makes the Browser a Compute Node
item.description: When the tab can run serious GPU work, the architecture question is not 'can we?' It is 'should this run next to the user's passwords, and what is the fallback?'

item.title: AI-Augmented Engineering Without Outsourcing Judgment
item.description: How Claude and Cursor can compress design, coding, and review cycles while keeping architecture and production decisions human-owned.

item.title: Reusable AEM Components That Actually Reduce Authoring Work
item.description: Lessons from enterprise Adobe Experience Manager delivery on making component libraries useful for authors, not just developers.

item.title: Cutting System Load Time from 15 Seconds to 2 Seconds
item.description: A practical account of performance work on a high-availability insurance technology platform: find the critical path, measure, then simplify.

item.title: Lessons from Serverless ETL on AWS
item.description: What matters when Lambda, S3, and Step Functions process high-volume data under production SLAs.
